title: Derived base-change map for a commutative square of ringed topoi
statement:
Let $\mathcal E,\mathcal E',\mathcal F,\mathcal F'$ be Grothendieck topoi in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-topos, def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings $A_{\mathcal E},A_{\mathcal E'},A_{\mathcal F},A_{\mathcal F'}$. Give a commutative square of ringed-topos morphisms [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]
$$\begin{array}{ccc}(\mathcal E',A_{\mathcal E'})&\xrightarrow{g'}&(\mathcal E,A_{\mathcal E})\\ f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\(\mathcal F',A_{\mathcal F'})&\xrightarrow{g}&(\mathcal F,A_{\mathcal F}),\end{array}$$
including compatible structural ring maps and a specified inverse-image square identification. For each corner $\mathcal V$, put $D_{\mathcal V}=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_{\mathcal V}))$, the ordinary derived category of sheaves of modules over that corner's ring [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every edge $a:(\mathcal V,A_{\mathcal V})\to(\mathcal W,A_{\mathcal W})$, use module pullback $a^*M=A_{\mathcal V}\otimes_{a^{-1}A_{\mathcal W}}a^{-1}M$ and module direct image $a_*$ with its structural $A_{\mathcal W}$-action [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Use their total derived functors $La^*:D_{\mathcal W}\to D_{\mathcal V}$ and $Ra_*:D_{\mathcal V}\to D_{\mathcal W}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], their standard derived adjunction $La^*\dashv Ra_*$ [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], and the canonical composition identification induced by the specified ringed-topos square [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]
$$\theta:Lf'^*Lg^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg'^*Lf^*\quad\text{of functors }D_{\mathcal F}\to D_{\mathcal E'}.$$
Explicitly, let $p=g\circ f\prime$ and $q=f\circ g\prime$, let $c_{f\prime,g}:Lp^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf\prime{}^*Lg^*$ and $c_{g\prime,f}:Lq^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg\prime{}^*Lf^*$ be those composition comparisons, and let $\delta:Lp^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lq^*$ be induced by the specified ring-compatible square identification. Use $\theta=c_{g\prime,f}\circ\delta\circ c_{f\prime,g}^{-1}$. The derived base-change morphism for $K\in D_{\mathcal E}$ is the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]
$$\beta_K:Lg^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*Lg'^*K\quad\text{in }D_{\mathcal F'},$$
whose transpose under $Lf'^*\dashv Rf'_*$ is
$$Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\theta_{Rf_*K}}Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{Lg'^*\varepsilon_{f,K}}Lg'^*K.$$
Here $\varepsilon_f:Lf^*Rf_*\to\mathrm{id}_{D_{\mathcal E}}$ is the counit. Equivalently $\beta_K$ is the unit $\eta_{f',Lg^*Rf_*K}$ followed by $Rf'_*(\theta_{Rf_*K})$ and then $Rf'_*Lg'^*(\varepsilon_{f,K})$. For abelian sheaves, take the constant sheaf of rings $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal V}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] at each corner, with the canonical constant-scalar inverse-image identifications of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Under the canonical identification of $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal V}$-module sheaves with abelian sheaves (integer multiplication gives the action, and determines it uniquely), module pullback is the exact abelian inverse image of that lemma. Its termwise functor is its total left derived functor [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Thus termwise inverse images replace $La^*$ in the same formulas, and each $D_{\mathcal V}$ is $D(\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal V))$.
